provenance.test: default activation_type (relu), one expert per token
provenance.notes: Exercises the schema's default activation with no optional biases or FC3 input.

provenance.test: activation_type gelu with an FC1 bias
provenance.notes: Tanh-approximate GELU after the FC1 projection and its per-expert bias.

provenance.test: activation_type silu at k = 2 with an FC2 bias
provenance.notes: The FC2 bias belongs to the expert, so at k = 2 each selected expert contributes its own bias scaled by its own routing weight. Adding it once to the routed sum instead would be wrong by the difference of the two experts' biases.

provenance.test: activation_type silu with FC3 as a multiplicative linear projection
provenance.notes: The pinned CUDA provider's separate FC3 gated-MLP form computes the FC3 projection times SiLU of the FC1 projection.

provenance.test: all three optional biases present at once
provenance.notes: The SiLU gated path applies FC1, FC2, and FC3 biases in one invocation.
One fused FC1 whose row block holds the gate half then the linear half. inter_size is the FC1 row count halved, which is what fusion_size 2 means in the schema's shape formula.

The same fused FC1 as fusion 2 but with the two operands interleaved: lane i reads rows 2i and 2i+1 rather than i and inter+i. Reading the concatenated layout here still lands on the right gate row for lane 0 and on the wrong linear row for it, and on the wrong row for both operands of every later lane.

With the GEMMs unfused the SwiGLU operands come from separate FC1 and FC3 tensors, so fusion_size is 1 and inter_size is the full FC1 row count. FC3 is required in this form and rejected in the fused ones.

swiglu_limit clamps the gate operand from above and the linear operand into [-limit, limit] before the product. The limit is small enough here that it actually binds; when the attribute is absent no clamp is applied at all.
num_tokens is the product of every leading dimension, so a [1, 3, 4] input routes exactly like the [3, 4] case while the output keeps the 3D shape.

provenance.test: k equal to the expert count
provenance.notes: Every expert is selected for every token, which is the upper bound the contract allows and the case where the router's taken-exclusion has to visit every index without repeating one.
A zero-length token axis: every stage dispatches nothing and the output is empty. The route scratch is still allocated at one element so the binding stays well-formed.
